title: Support landscape and iPad
description: Turn on landscape and iPad in NativePHP's config, and use Firstlight's Android tab bar so tabs get out of the way of the keyboard and short landscape screens.

blocks.text: NativePHP apps are portrait-only on phones until you say otherwise. Firstlight controls lay out in every orientation and on iPad, so turning these on is a config change plus one line for the Android tab bar.

runs.text: on Android. NativePHP's default allows portrait only:

blocks.text:
'orientation' => [
    'iphone' => [
        'portrait' => true,
        'upside_down' => false,
        'landscape_left' => true,
        'landscape_right' => true,
    ],
    'android' => [
        'portrait' => true,
        'upside_down' => true,
        'landscape_left' => true,
        'landscape_right' => true,
    ],
],
The change takes effect in the next build.

blocks.text: Once an App Store version supports iPad, later versions can't drop it, and App Review needs iPad screenshots. Decide before you upload.
On iPad, Firstlight uses the regular-width presentations: Date Picker, Time Picker and Select open as popovers next to their field, and Confirmation Dialog is a centred alert with both actions.

use-firstlights-tab-bar-on-android.title: Use Firstlight's tab bar on Android

blocks.text: On Android, NativePHP draws a layout's tabs as Material's 80 dp navigation bar. It stays above the keyboard, so it can cover the field being edited, and in landscape it and the app bar leave little room for content. Select Firstlight's tab bar in your layout instead:
NativePHP still owns the tabs, selection, badges and navigation. Firstlight draws the bar the way Material recommends:

items.label: Bar
items.text: Hidden, so the field stays visible

blocks.text: Date Picker and Time Picker on a short Android screen put the header beside the calendar and the time beside the clock dial, in a dialog that fits the screen and scrolls, with Cancel and Confirm always visible. iPhone keeps a sheet sized to the picker.
The Media crop sheet puts its controls beside the image.
Bottom Sheet detents don't apply on a phone in landscape: iOS shows the sheet at full height.
